intro: London is smaller than it looks and the transport is better than you have been told. Three things and you will move around like you live here.

cards.title: Just tap your card
cards.body: No Oyster card, no ticket machine, no queue. Tap the same contactless card or phone you use at home on the yellow reader. Tube: tap in and tap out — miss the tap out and you are charged the maximum fare. Buses: tap on only. Everyone in your group needs their own card.
cards.detail: Zones 1–2 cap at £8.90 a day, zones 1–3 at £10.50 — once you hit it, the rest of the day is free.

cards.title: Use a no-fee card
cards.body: Most US cards work fine, but many banks add a foreign transaction fee to every single tap — which turns a £2.80 tube ride into a line item you will regret. Travel cards without foreign fees are the fix. Load one into Apple Pay or Google Pay and tap with your phone.
cards.detail: Same card all day, every day — the daily cap only works if it recognises you.

cards.title: Download Citymapper
cards.body: This is the one. Built in London, for London — it knows which end of the platform to stand at, which carriage exits nearest your stairs, when a line is part-suspended, and it will tell you when walking is genuinely faster. Google Maps is fine. Citymapper is better here.
cards.detail: Free, iOS and Android. Set it up on the plane.

cards.title: Black cab or Uber
cards.body: Uber works across London and is usually the cheaper of the two. Black cabs cost more but the drivers have passed The Knowledge — a three-year exam on every street in the city — and they take contactless. Orange light on means available; stick your arm out.
cards.detail: In central London at rush hour, the tube beats both. Every time.

cards.title: Walk more than you think
cards.body: Central London is deceptively compact. Covent Garden to Leicester Square is 4 minutes on foot and two stops with a change on the tube. If Citymapper says the walk is under 15 minutes, walk it — you will see more of the city that way than from a tunnel.
cards.detail: Stand on the right on escalators. Walk on the left. This is not optional.

cards.title: Getting back late
cards.body: The Night Tube runs Friday and Saturday nights on the Victoria, Central, Jubilee, Northern and Piccadilly lines. Night buses run every night and cost a fraction of a cab. Last regular tubes are around 00:30 — earlier than most Americans expect.
cards.detail: Match nights: check before you commit to a second round.
